Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Louise Schiavone.
Dozens of homes near a Royal Air Force base used by U.S. bombers remain evacuated after
five men were arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act.
Maggie Blythe, temporary chief constable for Gloucestershire Constabulary, says the Army's
Explosive Ordnance Disposal Unit continues to examine three vehicles near Wellford.
"I would want to ensure and reassure our communities that any call into us is always acted on and
any information or intelligence passed to the police, again, is treated really seriously.
We will continue to do that.
We already do, and the same would apply to my colleagues from other agencies."
RAF Fairford hosts the U.S. Air Force's 501st Combat Support Wing and has been used by the
U.S. for strikes on Iranian missile sites in the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran that began
on February 28th.
With the midterm election just over a month away, some Democrats are focusing on faith
as an issue that might sway voters to their side.
NPR's Jason Derose reports a noteworthy number of Democratic candidates are clergy.
In Texas, Baptist pastor Frederick Haines is running for an open U.S. House seat in
the Dallas area, and Presbyterian seminary student James Tallarico is the Democratic
nominee for Senate there.
A Methodist pastor is the Democratic Senate nominee in Kansas, and a Lutheran pastor and
a Presbyterian chaplain are running as Democrats for two different U.S. House seats in Iowa.
Pew Research has found that fewer than one third of Democrats say religion is important
to them, but communities vary widely, and these candidates appear to be gaining traction.
The Cook Political Report has moved the Texas Senate seat and one Iowa House district from
Leans Republican to toss-up.
Jason Derose, NPR News.
Researchers on Wall Street are bracing for the latest report card on the labor market
this week.
They're also watching for the Federal Reserve's Favorite Inflation Indicator.
NPR's Rafael Knott reports the data will come as the central bank is facing big decisions
on interest rates.
After raising interest rates this month, policymakers need to decide whether to raise them again
in order to bring down inflation.
A key factor will be the labor market, which has been remarkably sturdy this year.
If that trend continues when the latest numbers come out on Friday, it could give the Fed
more room to raise interest rates again.
After all, it's easier for households to absorb the impact of higher rates if people are employed.
In the week ahead, we'll also get the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index, a key
inflation gauge.
Rafael Knott, NPR News.
A hurricane watch has been lifted for Hawaii's Big Island local officials now taking stock
of the aftermath.
Several inches of rain fell across the Big Island yesterday, which led to flooding on
many roads.
Thousands started the day without power.
This is NPR News.
Detroit authorities say an early Sunday morning shooting at an after-hours strip club left
three dead and four injured.
Authorities say an argument devolved into gunfire.
Police responded to the scene shortly after 7 a.m. today.
They said all the victims were thought to be in their 20s and 30s.
The 2019 superhero epic Avengers Endgame is back atop box office charts this weekend,
and PR's Bob Mondello calls this encore edition a lucrative marketing gimmick.
Marvel will be opening Avengers Doomsday in three months, and what better way to promote
it than to bring back Endgame?
Avengers!
Assemble.
With four minutes of unseen footage to stoke excitement for the new installment, fans showed
up hoping to catch a glimpse of Robert Downey Jr., returning not as Iron Man but as a supervillain.
For I am doom.
This weekend's $86 million in ticket sales puts Endgame, the second biggest earner in
Hollywood history, within striking distance of Avatar, currently the biggest, and it edged
the total box office hall for the 38-film Marvel Cinematic Universe above $35 billion.
Bob Mondello, NPR News.
At the President's Cup golf tournament in Medina, Illinois, Americans took the trophy
for the 11th consecutive time.
President Trump, the tournament's honorary chairman, was on the first tee for the start,
rallies on the back nine by two-time major champion Colin Morikawa, and rookie Jackson
Koiva nailed the team's victory.
I'm Louise Schiavone, NPR News, Washington.
